Pallab Karmakar pushed all 10 commits on Oct 10 and 11 through PRs #6 and #7. Main is green: lint, `tsc --noEmit` and Vitest all pass (8 files, 74 tests). The headline: the reel pipeline went from picking pre-built Remotion templates to having the LLM write a new Remotion component for every video.

## What changed

**PR #6: research, theming and the v2 renderer** (7 commits)
- `app/types.ts` gets more types: `ReelTheme`, `TransitionType`, 24 visual archetypes, `narrationBeat`.
- New `server/search.ts` scrapes DuckDuckGo Lite and Wikipedia so the planner has facts about the topic before it writes a script.
- `aicredits.ts` now guesses a genre from the prompt and picks a theme palette. It asks for 6 to 20 scenes.
- `timeline.ts` moved from `app/remotion/` to `app/server/`. Scene length now follows how much speech each scene has, with a clamp so long reels can't produce negative slot lengths.
- The renderer got 19 visual components plus slide, wipe and flip transitions. It also added Attack on Titan anime JPGs under `app/public/assets/anime/`.

**PR #7: LLM-written visuals** (the big one)
- The pipeline is now voice first: TTS, then Whisper word timestamps, then scenes locked to beats, then a review pass, then a component generated for that one video.
- `server/codegen.ts` (new, 565 lines) runs that component through a chain: a regex security scan, `tsc`, a webpack bundle, a still-frame probe (`probe.png`), then the full render.
- `server/review.ts` checks AV sync, visual variety and whether the numbers match the research. Its warnings go to logs and `review.json`, not the UI.
- `server/eval.ts` scores each reel 1 to 5 on hook, variety, motion, sound and originality.
- `server/prompts.ts` now holds all the house style rules. Style changes go there and nowhere else.
- `app/remotion/` now holds only the stage. The PR #6 templates are gone again, and **no template fallback remains**. If codegen fails, the job fails.
- It vendored two skill packs (`motion-graphics`, `remotion-best-practices`). Those account for most of the 36k added lines, since they include sample map JSON files of 7.5k lines each.

## Things you should know

1. **The server now runs code an LLM wrote.** The guard is a regex denylist (`codegen.ts:84-101`) plus an import allowlist (react, remotion, @remotion/shapes). Regex scans are easy to slip past. For example, `globalThis["fe"+"tch"]` or `window.Function` would not match `fetch(` or `eval(`. Search results feed the prompt, so a poisoned web page could steer the generated code. On a local dev tool that's probably fine. Before anyone else can reach this server, it needs real sandboxing.
2. **`index.ts` now catches `uncaughtException` and only logs it.** Node keeps running in an unknown state. Logging and then exiting is the usual pattern.
3. **New optional env var: `TRANSCRIBE_MODEL`** (default `openai/whisper-1`). If your gateway rejects Whisper, timings fall back to estimates. Add it to `.env.example` if you keep one.
4. **New dependency: `@remotion/shapes` with `^4.0.534`.** Every other `@remotion/*` package is pinned exactly. Remotion wants all its packages on the same version, so a caret here can drift and break the bundle.

Your setup is fine. The `remotion:render` npm script is stale, and PR #7 broke it.

## Why it throws

Since PR #7, `GeneratedReel` no longer draws any visuals. It's only the stage: audio, timeline, transitions, grain. Each scene's content comes from an LLM-written component, passed in through React context (`GeneratedReel.tsx:31-35`):

```tsx
const CustomVisualContext = createContext<GeneratedVisualComponent | null>(null);
const useCustomVisual = () => useContext(CustomVisualContext);
```

Only the per-job entry file fills that context. `codegen.ts:283` writes the file to `reel/<jobId>/entry.generated.tsx`, and it wraps the reel like this:

```tsx
<CustomVisualProvider value={GeneratedVisual}>
  <GeneratedReel {...props} />
</CustomVisualProvider>
```

Your script runs `remotion render remotion/index.tsx GeneratedReel ...`. That bare entry registers `GeneratedReel` with no provider around it, so `useCustomVisual()` returns `null` and line 233 throws. The message blames codegen, but codegen never ran. Pallab removed the template fallback on purpose so a failed job can't ship filler. The side effect is that a reel with no injected component can't render at all, and that includes this manual script.

It got past review because the script still bundles, and no test runs it.

## How to render now

- **To check the pipeline works:** `npm run render:smoke`. It writes a small hand-made component into `reel/smoke/`, builds an entry with the real `buildEntrySource()`, and renders through the same `renderReel` path that jobs use. It calls no paid APIs.
- **To re-render a real job:** `npx remotion render reel/<jobId>/entry.generated.tsx JobReel out.mp4`. Note the composition ID is `JobReel` (`codegen.ts:21`), not `GeneratedReel`. Your current `reel/` folders all come from Oct 10, before PR #7, so none of them has an `entry.generated.tsx` yet. A new job through the UI will create one.

## What I'd do with the script

You can either delete `remotion:render` or repoint it. I'd delete it. `render:smoke` already covers "render something by hand to see it work," and re-rendering a job needs a job ID that a fixed npm script can't hold. `remotion:studio` also points at the bare `remotion/index.tsx`, so it will show the same error on any frame. It will run and produce a reel, but three parts of your brief go against how the pipeline is built right now. I checked the code paths that handle each of them.

## What will work

- **20 seconds.** The planner reads "20-second" from the prompt, sets a word budget of about 50 words (at 2.5 words per second), and adjusts TTS speed to fit.
- **Botanical illustrations and clean type.** The codegen step writes React with inline SVG, so it can draw leaves, petals and bottles from scratch, and the type rules in `prompts.ts` already push toward clean layouts.
- **"Like cures like" fits easily in under 20 seconds.**

## What will fight you

**1. You'll get a dark background with neon accents, not pastels.** All six themes in `THEME_PALETTES` (`aicredits.ts:286`) use a near-black base, and the stage backgrounds in `GeneratedReel.tsx` run from `#05070A` to `#141211`. Your prompt contains none of the theme keywords, so it falls into `education`: navy-black with neon green, blue and yellow. `extractUserColors` only knows about saturated colors like neon and crimson, so "pastel" has no effect. `prompts.ts:26` does tell codegen to use light mode "only when the brief asks," and your brief asks. So the generated layer may paint a pastel scene on top while the dark stage shows through at the edges and during crossfades. Expect a mix of the two.

**2. The script prompt pushes hard toward high energy.** The scriptwriter's system prompt (`aicredits.ts:538-546`) says "high-voltage," "shocking contrast," "high-energy & punchy" and names Fireship as the model. Your "calming, educational vibe" goes up against those rules, and system prompts usually win. Expect a punchy hook, not a gentle one.

**3. "Bloom and transform into bottles" won't be a true shape morph.** Codegen may only import `react`, `remotion` and `@remotion/shapes` (`codegen.ts:262`). Real SVG path morphing needs `interpolatePath` from `@remotion/paths`, which isn't allowed. The model will fake it with a crossfade, scale or mask. That can look fine, but it won't be one shape flowing into another.

## One content flag

Before writing the script, the pipeline searches Wikipedia and DuckDuckGo, and Wikipedia describes homeopathy as a pseudoscience with no effect beyond placebo. That goes into the script prompt, so the voiceover might hedge or contradict your framing. Separately, platforms flag health claims, and a reel that presents "like cures like" as proven medicine is the kind they flag. The origin story is solid ground: mother tinctures are real plant extracts steeped in alcohol. Phrasing it as "homeopathy is built on the idea that like cures like" explains the principle without claiming it works, and it keeps the reel factual.

## What I'd do

**Option A, just try it (about 5 minutes).** Add these lines to your prompt to lean on everything a prompt can control:

> Light pastel background (cream, sage, blush, lavender), not dark mode. Slow, gentle narration with a soft opening line, no shock hook. Leaves unfold petal by petal, then cross-dissolve into an amber dropper bottle.

This makes problem 1 less likely and softens problem 2. It doesn't fix either.

**Option B, fix it properly (about 1 to 1.5 hours with tests).** Add a light `wellness` theme with a pastel palette and a matching stage background, route words like pastel, calm, soothing, herbal and homeopathic to it, and let the theme change the scriptwriter's tone rules. That's the long-term fix, and it would help every soft or lifestyle reel, not only this one. It also changes Pallab's pipeline, so it's worth a quick check with him first.

My suggestion: run Option A once to see the baseline, then decide on B with the actual reel in hand.

I traced the failure to its cause: one line in the codegen contract hands the model an `any` type. Here's how that breaks the run.

## Why it failed

The error is `visual.generated.tsx(586,101): TS18046: 'h' is of type 'unknown'`. The line in question:

```tsx
// line 533
const highlightSet = new Set(p.visualData.highlightWords ?? []);
// line 586
Array.from(highlightSet).some(h => h.includes(cleanWord))  // h: unknown
```

The model's logic is fine. The type is what breaks. `prompts.ts:87` gives the model this exact Props line to copy:

```ts
visualData: Record<string, any>
```

So `p.visualData.highlightWords` is `any`. When you pass `any` to `new Set(...)`, TypeScript can't infer the element type and settles on `Set<unknown>`. Then `h` is `unknown`, and calling `.includes` on it fails under `strict: true`. It's a well-known TypeScript quirk: an `any` going into a generic constructor comes out as `unknown`. The real type already exists as `SceneVisualData` in `types.ts:62`, with `highlightWords?: string[]`. The generated file can't import it, because the scan only allows `react`, `remotion` and `@remotion/shapes`. So the prompt falls back to `any`.

The repair round got the error back and still failed. With a 607-line file, the model probably rewrote the wrong part or kept the same pattern. Your prompt didn't cause this, and any reel that highlights keywords can hit it. Your pastel and gentle-tone lines worked as far as the job got: the plan, script and voice all finished.

## Three other things in that log

1. **"Resubmit to retry, the voice, transcript, and plan are intact" is misleading.** No resume path exists in `jobs.ts`. Resubmitting starts a new job and pays for research, script, TTS and planning all over again.
2. **The research query is your prompt minus the first two words.** `extractSearchQuery` (`search.ts:26`) only strips patterns like "create a 20-second reel about". Your prompt says "Create a 20-second visually soothing animated reel...", which doesn't match, so it searched for the long sentence and the facts it found are probably weak. Also, `search.ts:244` adds `"wallpaper character anime art"` to the image search for every topic, homeopathy included. That's left over from the Attack on Titan work.
3. **Your gateway doesn't return Whisper word timestamps.** It fell back to estimated timings as designed. Sync will be close, but not locked to the actual words.

## What I'd do

**Fix the contract (about 20 to 30 minutes with a test).** In `prompts.ts:87`, replace `Record<string, any>` with an inline copy of the `SceneVisualData` fields, since the model can't import the type. Then `highlightWords` arrives as `string[]` and this kind of failure goes away. Add one test that runs the codegen `tsc` gate on a component using this exact `new Set(p.visualData.highlightWords ?? [])` pattern, so a regression would fail CI instead of costing you a paid run. The smoke fixture in `render-smoke.ts:12` copies the same `any` line and should change with it.

type Equal<A, B> = (<T>() => T extends A ? 1 : 2) extends (<T>() => T extends B ? 1 : 2) ? true : false;

content.text:
Agreed. Here's what's actually wrong, ranked by how much each cause contributes. Without that, any fix is a guess.

## Why it looks like this

**1. A small model writes the visuals.** `generateVisualCode` (`aicredits.ts:779`) uses `config.videoModel`, and your `.env` sets that to `openai/gpt-4.1-mini`. That one model writes the script, the plan and a 600-line animated React component in a single shot, under about ten pages of rules. Mini models handle the first two fine. The third is hard, and the output shows it. The prompt already says:
- "SVG FIRST: every beat draws its concept as real vector graphics... Plain paragraphs on a black background are a FAILED beat" (`prompts.ts:45`)
- "Sizing floor: hero ≥56px, labels ≥26px" (`prompts.ts:72`)

The model wrote **one `<svg>` with two `<path>`s for the whole reel**, and font sizes of **20 to 36px** on a 1080×1920 canvas. It ignored both rules. That's why you mostly hear voice over near-empty frames.

**2. Nothing enforces those rules.** The scan only rejects a component with zero SVG (`codegen.test.ts:36`), so one SVG passes. Nothing checks font sizes. The output met the letter of the gates and failed everything else.

**3. The pipeline hands the model a dashboard.** The choreographer picks template-era archetypes (`bento_grid`, `comparison_matrix`). The review step then forces data-visual rules on them and rebuilds payloads by chopping up the voiceover. That's where "Following principle like / cures" came from. The codegen prompt puts `intent=bento_grid` and that payload on every beat (`codegen.ts:68`). Your "botanical illustration" brief never reaches the model as a scene type.

**4. Dark mode is hardcoded in three places.** `CANVAS_LAW` (`prompts.ts:25`) lists "near-black #0B0D12" under "CANVAS FACTS (non-negotiable)". All six theme palettes are dark. So is the stage background. Your "not dark mode" line loses three to one.

So it's not one bug. Pallab's v3 design is sound in shape (LLM writes bespoke code, then gates check it). But as wired, it gives a small model a bad brief, accepts weak output, and can't do light mode.

## What I'd do

Don't rewrite the pipeline yet. Run one experiment first to find out how much of this is the model.

**Experiment (about 30 minutes, one paid codegen call):** write a small script that loads this job's existing plan from disk and re-runs only codegen with a stronger model, then renders. The voice, transcript and plan stay the same, and only the model changes. If the result is clearly better, the main fix is a separate `CODEGEN_MODEL` env var, so the cheap model keeps doing script and plan and the strong one writes visuals. That's about 15 minutes. If it's still bad, causes 3 and 4 are the real blockers, and we fix the pipeline knowing that.

After that, in order:
- **Light theme plus dropping the hardcoded dark colors:** about 1 to 1.5 hours.
- **Static checks** for SVG count per beat and minimum font size, so weak output triggers the repair round instead of passing: about 45 minutes.
- **Letting illustration briefs skip data archetypes:** a choreographer redesign, so that one needs Pallab.

For the experiment I need one fact from you, because the gateway decides which models exist: which stronger models does your AICredits account serve? Something like `openai/gpt-4.1`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` or `openai/o4-mini`. I'd pick the best code model available, since this job is mostly writing correct React and SVG.

**Next action:** check your AICredits dashboard or model list for the strongest code model you can use, and paste its exact ID here (2 minutes).

It won't come close to that. Codegen is **one LLM call per reel**, or two if the repair round runs, and only that one step would change models. Script, plan and review stay on `gpt-4.1-mini`. I measured this job's actual codegen call:

- **Input:** 13,900 chars of prompt, about **3.5k tokens**
- **Output:** 14,860 chars of code, about **5k tokens** (the hard cap is 16k)

At the prices on the AICredits page:

| Model | Per codegen call | With repair round | Worst case (16k out + repair) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `openai/gpt-4.1-mini` (current) | ~$0.01 | ~$0.02 | ~$0.06 |
| `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` | **~$0.003** | ~$0.006 | ~$0.02 |
| `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` | ~$0.06 (about ₹5) | ~$0.11 | ~$0.35 |

So Sonnet adds roughly **5 to 10 cents per reel**, not dollars. Output tokens drive the cost, and at 5k per call there aren't many.

**Something I didn't expect:** `claude-haiku-5.5` is listed at $0.10/$0.50, which is **cheaper than the mini model you use now**, by about 3x. I don't know yet whether it writes better visuals than `gpt-4.1-mini`. It could beat it, or it could tie. Either way it's worth one test, because a win there costs you nothing.

**Avoid for this job:** the `codex` and `o`-series models. They bill hidden reasoning tokens on top of the visible output, so their real cost per call can be several times what the price table suggests.

## Revised experiment

Both findings are real. They're in Pallab's new `manim-service`, not in anything I wrote, so I've only verified them and haven't changed anything.

**1. Critical: the Manim service runs LLM-written Python with no sandbox** (`manim_runner.py:508-525`).
- The LLM's script gets written to disk and run with `create_subprocess_exec`.
- Nothing checks the code first: no AST check and no import allowlist. The Remotion version at least had the regex scan.
- No `env=` is passed, so the child process inherits the container's whole environment. `docker-compose.yml` loads `./app/.env` into it, which includes `AICREDITS_API_KEY`. Generated code can read your key and send it anywhere.
- The service publishes port `8000:8000` on all interfaces and has no authentication. Anyone who can reach that port can submit a prompt.

Docker limits the damage to the container, but your key is inside the container.

**2. High: stored XSS in the service UI** (`static/app.js:134` and `:170`). `job.error`, `j.title` and `j.prompt` go into `innerHTML` without escaping. The prompt is user input, and the error can include LLM-generated text, so a crafted prompt can run script in the browser of anyone who opens the job list. The fix is to build those nodes with `textContent`, about 15 minutes.

What I'd tell Pallab, most important first:
1. Bind the port to localhost: `"127.0.0.1:8000:8000"` (1 minute).
2. Pass only `PATH` and `HOME` to the render subprocess, and give the Manim container its own env file with no API keys (about 15 minutes).
3. Fix the XSS (about 15 minutes).
4. Add an AST allowlist for the generated scripts (about 1 hour).

This is the same issue I flagged after the first pull, now in Python. It matters more here, because a Python subprocess can do far more than a webpack-bundled React component.

None of this changes the decision you owe me on the commit.

content.text:
Good thing I checked. **The Manim service's main LLM isn't AICredits.** It calls a separate LiteLLM gateway (`litellm.vision.aivar.app`, per `manim-service/.env.example`). AICredits is only the last fallback, on `gpt-4.1-mini`, which is fast enough to finish under the cutoff. So the timeout problem matters much less to Pallab than I said, and I've rewritten that section to match. Here's the draft:

---

Hey Pallab, I went through the Manim migration after pulling. I pushed three small fixes to `main` and have a few things for you.

**What I pushed** (`7310b45..dc403f5`):
- Deleted the 7 `app/server/*.test.ts` files. They import `vitest`, which you removed, so `tsc --noEmit` failed with 8 errors.
- Removed the `react` import from `app/types.ts` (only the dead `GeneratedVisualComponent` used it).
- Regenerated `app/package-lock.json`. It still listed Remotion, React, Vitest and ESLint, so `npm ci` installed the old tree. The packages we kept stay at the same versions.
- `npm run dev` now runs `tsx watch`, so it restarts when server files change.

**Dead code left in `app/`** (I didn't delete it, it's your call):
- `server/aicredits.ts`, `eval.ts`, `media.ts`, `review.ts`, `search.ts`, `sound.ts`, `timeline.ts`, `prompts.ts`, `errors.ts`. Nothing imports them anymore. `index.ts` only uses `config` and `jobs`.
- `eslint.config.js` and `vitest.config.ts`, which point at packages that are no longer installed.
- The Remotion-era types in `types.ts`, such as `GeneratedVisualProps` and `SceneVisualData`.

**Security issues in `manim-service`** (most urgent first):
1. **LLM-written Python runs with no sandbox.** `manim_runner.py:508-525` writes the generated script to disk and runs it with `create_subprocess_exec`. Nothing checks the code first, and there's no `env=`, so it inherits the container env. `docker-compose.yml` loads `./app/.env` into the container, which means generated code can read `LLM_API_KEY` and `AICREDITS_API_KEY` and send them anywhere. A prompt injection through the user prompt is enough. Fixes:
   - Pass only `PATH` and `HOME` to the subprocess.
   - Give the Manim container its own env file, with only the keys it needs.
   - Longer term: AST-check the script, allow only `manim`, `numpy` and `math` imports, and block `open`, `exec`, `eval`, `__import__` and dunder access.
2. **Port 8000 is public with no auth.** Compose publishes `8000:8000` on all interfaces, and `/api/jobs` has no authentication, so anyone who can reach the machine can make it run LLM code. Quick fix: `"127.0.0.1:8000:8000"`, or no published port at all, with the app reaching it over the compose network.
3. **Stored XSS in `static/app.js`.** Lines 134 and 170 put `job.error`, `j.title` and `j.prompt` into `innerHTML` unescaped. The prompt is user input and the error can carry LLM text, so a crafted prompt runs script for anyone who opens the job list. Build those nodes with `textContent` instead.

Rough times: 1 minute for the port, about 15 minutes each for the env lockdown and the XSS, about an hour for the AST allowlist.

**AICredits gateway limits** (relevant to your last fallback in `llm_client.py`):
- The gateway cuts requests off at about 30s on `aicredits.in/v1` (bare HTTP 500) and about 60s on `api.aicredits.in/v1`.
- A cut-off request comes back 200 with `finish_reason: "length"` and no content, and it's still billed in full. `stream: true` doesn't help, because the gateway buffers the stream.
- I paid ₹9.40 for an empty Sonnet 5.5 reply learning this.
- Your fallback uses `gpt-4.1-mini`, which is fast enough to fit, so you're fine for now. But don't move that fallback to a slower model (Sonnet, Opus, reasoning models) for long outputs. Also, `llm_client.py` sets `timeout=120.0`, and on AICredits that's effectively 30 or 60.
- I've asked their support about raising the limit and will tell you what they say.

---

What I changed from my earlier summary:
- **The gateway section is narrower.** It now says only the AICredits fallback is affected, and warns against putting a slower model there, instead of implying the whole service is at risk.
- **The key exposure covers both keys.** The subprocess inherits `LLM_API_KEY` as well as `AICREDITS_API_KEY`.
- **The 120s client timeout is new.** `llm_client.py` sets it, and on AICredits the gateway cuts requests off well before that.

**Next action:** paste the message to Pallab (2 minutes).
